claims.text: The onset of premelting in HEA nanoparticles is primarily governed by enhanced surface segregation.
High configurational entropy drives enhanced surface segregation in HEA nanoparticles.
Surface segregation lowers the effective surface energy of HEA nanoparticles.
Lower effective surface energy promotes surface atomic rearrangements.
Segregation-mediated surface rearrangements cause HEA nanoparticles to begin premelting earlier than conventional binary or monometallic nanoparticles.
The relevant initial material is a compositionally disordered HEA nanoparticle population with a narrow size distribution in the approximate range of 5–20 nm.
Particle size and alloy complexity can be tested independently by comparing size-matched HEA and conventional binary nanoparticles under identical thermal-processing conditions.
Surface premelting occurs below the bulk melting point in a material-dependent temperature interval.
Redistribution of surface atoms modifies the effective surface energy of the nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy promotes selective surface segregation of lower-melting-point elements.
Selective enrichment by lower-melting-point elements reduces surface free energy.
Reduced surface free energy enhances atomic mobility at the nanoparticle surface.
Enhanced surface atomic mobility results in earlier premelting relative to nanoparticles with less compositional disorder.
Size-matched HEA nanoparticles will have a significantly lower premelting-onset temperature than conventional binary nanoparticles.
The reduction in premelting-onset temperature will be more pronounced for smaller nanoparticles because they have a higher surface-to-volume ratio.
Surface enrichment in specific elements will be measurable before bulk melting.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold for nanoparticles approximately 5–20 nm in size.
The proposed relationship may not extend to larger bulk-like particles or systems with extreme compositional imbalance.
Particle shape, experimental imperfections, and secondary-phase formation could modulate the observed premelting behavior.
